fixtures: lab-target golden rootfs (planted device surface in lab/target/start-services.sh and lab/target/notes/)

findings.control: device management plane: implementation and version disclosure
findings.rationale: The device's SSH management plane on tcp/22 hands its implementation and version to any unauthenticated prober in the handshake banner, giving an attacker free target-selection intelligence for the administrative surface.
findings.traces_to: lab/target/start-services.sh, the /usr/sbin/sshd listener on tcp/22 (banner observed by the zgrab2 ssh grab)

findings.rationale: Both administrative web planes (tcp/8000 and tcp/8080) serve their interfaces over cleartext HTTP with no TLS anywhere on the device's admin surface, so management interactions and responses travel unencrypted.
findings.traces_to: lab/target/start-services.sh, the two python3 -m http.server listeners on tcp/8000 and tcp/8080

findings.control: device config artifacts: operational documentation exposure
findings.rationale: The device's served tree exposes an operational redeploy checklist through an auto-indexed directory: the document inventories the device's listeners and its rotation procedure, disclosing configuration facts an attacker would otherwise have to probe for.
findings.traces_to: lab/target/notes/redeploy-checklist.txt, reachable via the indexless /notes/ directory listing on tcp/8000

findings.control: device inventory: offline image vs live surface reconciliation
findings.rationale: Reconciliation verdict, not a violation: the offline image's declared service set (ssh/22, http/8000, http/8080 in start-services.sh) matches the live probe exactly - no listener outside the image's declared set was observed, and no declared listener was dark.
findings.traces_to: lab/target/start-services.sh (declared set) reconciled against the live nmap port inventory of the spawned target
